ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, point D is on the extension line of BC, DE $\perp$ AB at point E, and intersects AC at point F. If $\angle A = 35^\circ$ and $\angle D = 15^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle ACB$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $DE \perp AB$ and $\angle A=35^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle CFD = \angle AFE = 90^\circ - \angle A = 90^\circ - 35^\circ = 55^\circ$,\\
Also, since $\angle D = 15^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle ACB = \angle D + \angle CFD = 15^\circ + 55^\circ = \boxed{70^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is on the bottom side, D is to the right of C and B, C, D are collinear; AB is the left slanted side, AC connects from A to C; draw line DE from D toward the upper left, intersecting AB at E and AC at F, and there is a right-angle mark at E, indicating DE ⟂ AB. Reasoning: Because DE is perpendicular to AB, the angle between AB and DE is 90°. It is known that ∠A is the angle between AB and AC, equal to 35°, therefore the angle between AC and DE is 90° − 35° = 55°. At point F, ∠CFD is equal to this angle, so ∠CFD = 55°. Also because D is on the extension of BC, ∠CDF is exactly the ∠D = 15° given in the problem. In triangle CDF, ∠ACB is the exterior angle at point C, equal to the sum of the two non-adjacent interior angles: ∠ACB = ∠CFD + ∠CDF = 55° + 15° = 70°.
